Some of those non-scoring results deserve close attention: 3 metres from M50 Terry Lawton in the pole vault, Junior Galley and Said Chettati racing out every centimetre of the 3k together to finish within 2/10ths, and Dan Gomme and Martin Readhead winning their 400m races.
We've always said that Junior Galley is more suited to middle distance track work rather than marathons. With his turn of speed he should be running more 5ks and even 1500 metres.

A massive pb came from Junior Galley in 5k. He steadily became more confident as the race progressed and was boosted when he overtook club-mate and rival Owain Lewes who was suffering from the heat after going off with the leaders.
Only one tenth separated Alex Luce and Phil Carstairs in the 1500m while Said Chettati ran to his best ever in the 5k with Junior Galley taking 2nd in the 'B'.
Where was Leo Lyons, Junior Galley; and Jim Estall, normally so full of running and ready to wave back on hearing his name called from the sidelines, looked positively sombre.
The London marathon had taken place the week before and this took Paul Evans, Gary Staines, Jim Estall and Junior Galley out of the equation.

…eft to right: Michael Manning and daughter, Ray Foley, Mick Graham, 'Gerry' Adams, John Mather, Rob Harding,Paul Roche, Junior Galley, a yawning John Gladwin who's seen it all before, Stu' Paton, Pete Gilbey, Tony Binda, Colin Preston, Roger Alsop, Charlie Dickinson, Marlon Anderson, Bruce Barton, J…

Roger Alsop ran steadily for 27th, then a gap before Mike Nouch and Junior Galley in the late fifties. One more engine room runner here would have given the Belgrave team medals even without Chris Sweeney, but it was not to be and it was thanks to Tony Stone for completing the scoring six back in 185th position.

Then the already mentioned Belgrave vests stretched from the early twenties to the fifties with Junior Galley looking relaxed after his Caribbean holiday (perhaps a bit too relaxed) and Said Chettati, struggling hard against the effects of his fast for Ramadin.

The initial stage gave us a three-way Belgrave clash as Dave Pamah (preparing for the track season and with no recent form) battled with Junior Galley (well into marathon training but desperate to do the 12-Stage) and the spritely Dave Beaver.

In spite of cramping up badly Junior Galley lost only one place as Thames Valley got by. Forty-five year-old 'toughie' Pete Gilbey set out with Shaftesbury's international John Sherban on his shoulder, had him race past within seconds, but 14 minutes later came back home with the Shaftesbury man now…

Then there was Jim Estall - as fit as a flea - and a whole bunch of others who may well spring surprises: Marcello Bizio, Stu' Paton, Junior Galley, Mike Kazimierski ... who would close in our team on what we hoped would be a winning occasion?

Junior Galley was next up, suffering from lack of sleep after the arrival of a new baby Galley a few days earlier, and when a plucky Chas. Dickinson completed his stint we hovered just on the 20 mark.

Junior Galley had a most uncomfortable 1500m run when he found himself being overtaken by Rosa Kutty with just over a lap to go. She was intent on setting a ground record while Junior had a battle on his hands to avoid being beaten by a woman.
After two stages the 'B's were ahead by 1 second – was it possible that veteran Don could keep close enough to Junior Galley to give Ray a fighting chance?

In the face of this onslaught Tony Binda and Junior Galley could do little but restrict the damage to a minimum although Tony took 37 seconds off the time he recorded in 1996 as a member of the Belgrave veterans' team.

From that point on Herne Hill held all the aces with Simon Jones' 13:18, and Ian Munt's 12:56 putting them beyond the reach of the Belgrave outfit which nevertheless continued to draw away from the rest of the field of 39 teams thanks to determined running from Roger Alsop, Junior Galley and Dave Beaver.
Junior Galley (75) takes over from veteran Tony Binda (74). Junior has left his staff in charge at the record store to help the Bels to a Surrey 'gold'.
Dickinson, Junior Galley and Mike Kazimierski completed our 12 man team and here we must pay tribute to the men who didn't score but still turned out.

Graham Adams is coming back to fitness so Roger Alsop and Junior Galley were persuaded to make up the team. But as the gun was fired we were still only five in number and when the results were published later in the week we were amazed to find that Kevin Nash had run in the Hampshire event!

Kevin moved up two places before handing over to Junior Galley who dropped back one slot during his circuit. How this man runs on the grassy slopes without spikes we'll never know.
Paul Coughlan and Kevin Quinn made more conservative starts while Junior Galley, although much happier on tarmac, had "gone for it" in a big way.

Veteran Jim was offered the chance to switch with Junior Galley in the Bs but decided to go for it. A position of 25th was looked for but he gave us better than that and a time 2 seconds faster than last year.

Junior Galley, an old hand at the event, took it steady this year but was able to shepherd Wesley Minett to the finish in under 3 hours, helping him to improve upon his previous best by some fifteen minutes.
